No. 13.09.2024  02.
 1.
The petitioner is an accused in connection with Banigochha P.S. Case No.29 of 2024 corresponding to Special G.R. Case No.13 of 2024 for the offences punishable under Sections 363/366/376(2)(n) of the IPC read with Section 6 of the POCSO Act pending in the Court of the learned Additional Sessions Judge- cum-Special Judge under POCSO Act, Nayagarh.
The petitioner had approached the learned Additional Sessions Judge-cum-Special Court under the POCSO Act, Nayagarh in Special G.R. Case No.13 of 2024 praying for grant of bail.
The learned Court below vide its order dated 02.05.2024 rejected the bail application of the petitioner.
Being aggrieved, the petitioner has filed the present petition under Section 439 of the Cr.P.C. praying for enlargement on bail.

2. Learned counsel for the petitioner, on instruction from the petitioner, submits that, except the present bail application, no other bail application of the petitioner is pending in any other Court relating to the aforesaid F.I.R.
3.
The prosecution case is that, on 24.02.2024, the complainant reported at Banigochha P.S. that on 23.02.2024, his daughter was talking with the present petitioner in her mobile phone.
Her mother saw that and took away the mobile phone from her daughter.
Since then, her daughter is missing.
Her mother doubts that the present petitioner has kidnapped her daughter.

Hence, the F.I.R.
4.

The statements of the victim recorded under Sections 161 and 164 Cr. P.C. were extensively read Manoj Nayak @ Mani vs State Of Odisha .... Opp. Party on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/33674700/
1 over by the counsel for parties.

sentences.text: From perusal of the evidence collected by the police reveals that the petitioner, who is of 20 years old boy, has been in relationship with the victim girl, who is stated to be 17 years of age.
5. The victim girl got eloped with the present petitioner to different places and stayed with the petitioner.
During their stay, they had physical relationship.
Subsequently, the F.I.R. has been registered by the father of the victim.
The petitioner has been in custody since 18.03.2024.

6. Regard being had to nature of the accusation and statements of the victim recorded under Sections 161 & 164 Cr. P.C. and the period of custody of the petitioner since 18.03.2024, I am inclined to admit the petitioner on bail.

In the event the petitioner is found wanting for violation of any of the bail conditions imposed by this Court or the trial Court even on a single occasion, the prosecution is at liberty to move appropriate application before the Court below for cancellation of the concession of bail granted by this Court.
If such application is filed, the trial Court should decide the application on its own merit.
8. The BLAPL is accordingly disposed of.
(S.S. Mishra) Judge Subhasis Location: High Court of Orissa, Cuttack.
